title: Isolated experiment whose useful reviewed changes are later asked about, then merged by the human
source: Replay of experiment transcript 2026-09-28T16:46-19:12 (local time): 'include in scope those changes', 'are the changes in main already', merge of PR #124 after local review, 'what's the status of the work item'.
ground_truth: Minimal world: project tally on main with an empty project board, plus an initialized scratch Pinboard board at ../scratch-board (outside the project). The human (Sam) asks for a throwaway experiment tracked on the scratch board, not committing to merge. Everything the agent does is observable in the per-turn state snapshots. Before turn 4 the harness (acting as Sam) merges the experiment branch into origin/main with a merge commit; the hooks log records the merged branch head. Local main is not updated by that merge. Any review happened on the branch commits before that merge.

turns.human: I want to try a quick experiment. On a throwaway branch, make tally.sh skip lines that start with '#' so input files can carry comments, and add one sentence about it to docs/usage.md. Track it on the scratch Pinboard board at ../scratch-board instead of our real board, I don't want to clutter it. I'm not committing to merging this; I just want to see whether it's worth it. Have it reviewed like normal work.
Nice. Keep it where it is for now, it was just an experiment. You can close it out.
We probably learned something useful there, I suppose? Ok, I forgot if we are on a work item now. Can we include those comment changes in scope, in a worktree if we don't have one yet?
I went ahead and merged that branch into main on origin myself. So that change is reviewed and done now, right?
Ok, what's the status of the work item?
